Stretcher: 1. "O'Keeffe (white paint) 2. "200" (Alfred Stieglitz, graphite) 3. 87 / 1922" (Alfred Stieglitz, graphite). Backing: "Georgia O'Keeffe [wavy underline]" (black ink) 
(Source: Lynes, 1999)

cr_data.provenance: (Alfred Stieglitz, New York, NY); Reinhardt Galleries, New York, NY, 1923; Annie B. Jennings, New York, NY, 1931; Oilver B. James, New York, NY, bequest, 1938; Mabel Davis James, Phoenix, Arizona, gift, 1939; Edward Jacobsen, Phoenix, Arizona, gift, 1968 (Source: Lynes, 1999)
remarks_1999: Abiquiú Notebooks and Whitney Archive indicate, "Letter from Oliver B. James. . . 'We own. . . Apple. . . inherited from Miss Annie B. Jennings, who purchased the item in 1931 from Henry Reinhardt & Son.' This is probably the small green and pink apple which Miss O'Keeffe says was in the 1923 exh. at the Anderson Gals. and bought by Reinhardt Gallery. I have dated it the same years as 'Apples, Yellow Group' and 'The Green Apple,' which were also in the 1923 exhibition and dated by O'Keeffe 1921." Stretcher inscription 3 dates 1922 and indicates no. 87 in 1923 New York (Anderson). Downtown Gallery Archive dates 1921. Whitney Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks date c. 1921. (Source: Lynes, 1999)
remarks_post_1999: Lynes publication dates this work as 1921–1922, Phoenix Art Museum dates it as 1920–1922. (Source: Information provided for *Access O'Keeffe* from Phoenix Art Museum, 2025)

description: A lumpy green apple with hints of powdery pink and yellow sits at the center of the canvas on a pale blue and white plane. The apple casts a dark blue shadow over the flat surface.
